title: Go: Graceful Shutdown
description: Implement signal handling and graceful shutdown patterns for Go services using channels, context, and http.Server.Shutdown.

steps.title: Signal notification with channels
steps.description: Create a channel using `signal.Notify` to catch `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM`. Run a simple goroutine that prints ticks, then block on the signal channel. Print `"Shutting down"` when a signal is received using `fmt.Println`.
hints: Use a buffered channel (buffer 1) for signals

verification.failureMessage: Print 'Shutting down' when a signal is received.

steps.title: http.Server Shutdown
steps.description: Create an `http.Server` listening on `:8080` (simulated, just create the struct). Call `server.Shutdown(ctx)` with a context timeout of 5 seconds when a signal is received. Print `"Server shut down"` using `fmt.Println`.
hints: Create a context with 5s timeout: context.WithTimeout
Shutdown returns an error if context expires first

verification.failureMessage: Print 'Server shut down' after Shutdown completes.

steps.title: Context cancellation propagation
steps.description: Create a root context that cancels on signal using `signal.NotifyContext`. Pass the context to background workers. When cancelled, workers should stop and print `"Worker stopped"` using `fmt.Printf`. Use `ctx.Done()` in a select statement.
hints: signal.NotifyContext returns a context that cancels on signal
Workers select on ctx.Done() and work channels

verification.failureMessage: Print 'Worker stopped' for each worker when context is cancelled.

steps.title: Multiple signal handlers
steps.description: Implement different behavior for different signals: `SIGINT` triggers immediate shutdown (2s timeout), `SIGTERM` triggers graceful shutdown (10s timeout), and `SIGHUP` triggers config reload. Print which action is taken using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: Select on multiple signal cases in a for loop
Use a boolean flag to break out of the loop
SIGHUP typically triggers re-read of config

verification.failureMessage: Print the action taken for each signal type.

steps.title: WaitGroup for goroutine tracking
steps.description: Use `sync.WaitGroup` to track active goroutines. Start multiple workers with `wg.Add(1)`, each calling `wg.Done()` when finished. On shutdown signal, wait for all workers with `wg.Wait()` before calling `Shutdown`. Print completion using `fmt.Println`.
hints: wg.Add before go statement, wg.Done at end of goroutine
wg.Wait blocks until all Done calls
Place wg.Wait before server.Shutdown in shutdown sequence

verification.failureMessage: Print when all workers have completed.

steps.title: Full graceful shutdown manager
steps.description: Create a `ShutdownManager` struct with methods `Add(id string, closer func() error)`, `Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error`, and timeout support. Track multiple resources. Demonstrate adding resources and shutting them all down in reverse order. Print shutdown progress using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: Use a slice of (id, closer) pairs
Collect errors and continue shutdown even on failure

verification.failureMessage: Print each resource being shut down in order.
